A medical scribe works closely with healthcare providers to document clinical interactions in real time, ensuring accurate and detailed patient records. This role allows medical professionals to focus more on patient care by handling the documentation side of the encounter.

TASKS: Documenting real-time patient encounters during virtual or recorded consultations using Electronic Medical Records (EMRs) such as Epic, AthenaNet/AthenaHealth, Cerner, or NextGen Accurately capturing patient histories, physical exam findings, diagnostic impressions, treatment plans, and follow-up instructions Updating and maintaining charts, medication lists, allergies, and problem lists Assisting with administrative tasks such as templating notes and handling visit summaries Reviewing prior records to provide context for current visits Maintaining communication with providers for clarification and accuracy of documentation Ensuring all documentation is HIPAA-compliant and meets clinical and legal standards Demonstrating strong attention to detail and discretion in handling sensitive patient data Requirements QUALIFICATIONS: Must have excellent verbal and written English communication skills At least 1–2 years of experience as a medical scribe or in a clinical documentation role Familiar with medical terminologies and clinical workflows A healthcare-related degree is highly preferred Proficient with Google Workspace and/or Microsoft Office Experience with EMRs such as Epic, Cerner, or AthenaHealth is a plus HIPAA Certification is a plus Fast and accurate typing skills Strong attention to detail Organized and highly focused Open to working night shifts We are looking for a detail-oriented Medical Documentation Assistant to support the administrative operations of a growing outpatient drug and alcohol treatment organization.

This position focuses on reviewing patient records, identifying outdated or missing documentation, and ensuring Attendance Agreements and other required records remain accurate and up to date. This is a fully remote, behind-the-scenes administrative role with very little patient interaction.

Training will be provided, so previous behavioral health experience is not required. Key Responsibilities

Review patient records within the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system
Review Attendance Agreements to ensure they are current and accurate
Verify assigned counselors, therapy groups, required signatures, and other documentation
Identify outdated, incomplete, or incorrect patient records
Generate reports of records requiring updates
Notify the appropriate staff of missing or incorrect information
Track outstanding documentation until completed
Perform data entry and maintain organized patient records
Assist with general administrative tasks as needed

Strong attention to detail
Excellent organizational skills
Comfortable working with computers and spreadsheets
Accurate data entry skills
Ability to work independently
Strong written English communication skills

Healthcare experience is a plus but not required
Work Details

Full-time
Fully remote
Training provided
HIPAA training provided
Success in This Role
Success in this role means ensuring patient records are accurate, Attendance Agreements remain current, documentation is complete, and the clinical team can rely on clean, organized records. Details Originally posted on Himalayas

***THIS IS NOT A VIRTUAL POSITION, YOU MUST LIVE WITHIN OR BE WILLING TO RELOCATE WITHIN A COMMUTABLE DISTANCE OF THE DUTY LOCATION*** MAJOR DUTIES: Accompanies Licensed Independent Practitioners (LIPs) during each patient visit and documents/transcribes information in the Electronic Health Record (EHR) that transpires during the LIP's visit at the direction of the LIP.

Accurately and thoroughly documents medical visits and procedures as they are being performed by the physician. Prepares operative reports, makes phone calls, and conducts other clerical tasks as assigned.

Enters all aspects of the patient encounter into the EHR including the patient history, physical exam findings verbalized by the LIP, procedures, orders, and clinic encounters.

Facilitates efficient patient flow through the clinic by ensuring timely processing of orders, including referrals, tests, medications, and encounters, and by preparing and forwarding documentation to the LIP for review, approval, and signature.

Documents all aspects of the office visit (handwritten, electronic, or otherwise) in the EHR during the patient encounter with the LIP.

Organizes information consisting of, but not limited to, plan and patient instructions in the EHR, assists the LIP in navigating the EHR, and locates information for review (i.e. previous notes, reports, test results and laboratory results).

Records diagnostic results such as radiology interpretations and lab values, and enters medication orders, physical therapy orders, home exercises, educational handouts, work restrictions and other orders per LIP instruction. Ensures accuracy, spelling, punctuation and grammar in documentation prior to LIP review and approval.

Ensures records are prepared for treatment team review by providing previously ordered tests if appropriate, adequate forms for documentation by team, recent information profile for LIP to review and appropriate encounter form attached to the medical record, assembling medical information in correct sequential and chronological order.

Ensures appropriate forms are completed, accurate and signatures obtained for requests/release of medical information. Initiates action to request records from other facilities, both VA and non-VA, and obtains all medical records as requested by treatment team.

Assists treatment team in ensuring medical documentation complies with Joint Commission and other accreditation body requirements. Performs statistical data collection. Performs other related duties as assigned. Work Schedule: Intermittent - 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., or 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., or 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

NOTE: Intermittent employment is defined as non-fulltime employment in which employees serve under an excepted or competitive service appointment without a regularly scheduled tour of duty. A position with an intermittent work schedule is sporadic and unpredictable so that a tour of duty cannot be regularly scheduled in advance.

Intermittent positions offer health insurance only if the employee is expected to work at least 130 hours per month for at least 90 days. Recruitment & Relocation Incentives: Not authorized Critical Skills Incentive (CSI): Not approved
EXPERIENCE: At least one (1) year of progressively responsible clerical, office, or other work that indicates ability to acquire the particular knowledge and skills needed to perform the duties of the position to be filled (Data Transcriber - Medical Scribe).

OR EDUCATION: Successful completion of two (2) years of education above the high school level in an accredited institution. This education must have been obtained in an accredited business, secretarial or technical school, junior college, college or university.

OR COMBINATION: A combination of post-high school education in an accredited institution and general experience that demonstrates your ability to perform the duties of this position may be used to qualify for this position.

ADDITIONAL QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS: This position includes Selective Placement Factors (skill, knowledge, ability or other worker characteristic basic to - and essential for - satisfactory performance of the job). Selective Placement Factors are a prerequisite to appointment and represent minimum requirements for a position.

Applicants who do not meet it are ineligible for further consideration.

The Selective Placement Factors for this position are: Knowledge of medical terminology Experience performing transcription ensuring accuracy, spelling, punctuation and grammar utilizing a variety of computer applicants/software such as word processing, spreadsheet/database and/or audio-visual presentation software TYPING PROFICIENCY: This position requires the skills of a qualified typist.

In addition to meeting the experience and/or education requirements, you must be able to type at least 25 words per minute.

You will be rated on the following Competencies as part of the assessment questionnaire for this position: Attention to Detail Clinical Data Collection/Documentation Computer Skills Manages and Organizes Information Medical Information Writing IMPORTANT: A full year of work is considered to be 35-40 hours of work per week.

All experience listed on your resume must include the month and year start/end dates. Part-time experience will be credited on the basis of time actually spent in appropriate activities.

Applicants wishing to receive credit for such experience must indicate clearly the nature of their duties and responsibilities in each position and the number of hours a week spent in such employment.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Physical Requirements: The work is sedentary and does not require any special physical effort.

Some work may require walking and standing in conjunction with travel and attendance at meetings and conferences away from the work site. Employee may carry light items such as papers, books, and portable computer requirement.

The work often requires long hours to meet project deadlines and to devise corrective action and solutions to unexpected technical and/or management crises resulting in sometimes highly stressful work situations.
